.lk:hover{border-color:var(--faint);color:var(--ink);background:var(--hover)}
.lk svg.i{width:14px;height:14px;color:var(--mut)}
.lk .lock{font-size:11px;color:var(--mut);font-weight:500;border-left:1px solid var(--line);padding-left:6px;margin-left:2px}

/* tabs */
.tabs{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;margin-top:22px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);position:sticky;top:56px;z-index:30;background:var(--bg)}
.tab{position:relative;height:42px;padding:0 12px;border:0;background:none;font-size:14px;font-weight:500;color:var(--mut);cursor:pointer;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px}
.tab:hover{color:var(--ink)}
.tab[aria-selected=true]{color:var(--ink)}
.tab[aria-selected=true]::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:8px;right:8px;bottom:-1px;height:2px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--ink)}
.tabs .sp{flex:1}
.tabs .hint{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}

/* shell */
.shell{display:grid;grid-template-columns:248px minmax(0,1fr);gap:36px;padding:24px 0 40px;align-items:start}
.rail{position:sticky;top:122px}
.rail h2{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut);letter-spacing:.02em;padding:0 10px 8px}
.rail ol{list-style:none;padding:0;position:relative}
.rail li{position:relative}
.rail li+li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:19px;top:-9px;height:18px;width:1.5px;background:var(--line)}
.rail li.done+li::before{background:var(--ok-mk)}
.rb{display:grid;grid-template-columns:20px minmax(0,1fr);gap:1px 10px;align-items:center;width:100%;padding:8px 10px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:9px;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;color:var(--ink2)}
.rb:hover{background:var(--hover)}
.rb[aria-current=step]{background:var(--panel);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line),var(--sh);color:var(--ink)}
.rb .rt{font-size:14px;font-weight:500}
.rb .rs{grid-column:2;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
.rb svg.i{width:18px;height:18px;position:relative;z-index:1;background:var(--bg);border-radius:50%}
.rb[aria-current=step] svg.i{background:var(--panel)}
.rail .meter{margin:16px 10px 0;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.rail .meter i{display:block;height:4px;border-radius:4px;background:var(--line2);margin-top:6px;overflow:hidden}
.rail .meter b{display:block;height:100%;background:var(--acc);border-radius:4px;transition:width .3s var(--ease)}

/* status icons */
.s-ok{color:var(--ok)}.s-bad{color:var(--bad)}.s-warn{color:var(--warn-dot)}.s-skip,.s-q{color:var(--faint)}.s-acc{color:var(--acc)}
.spin{animation:spin .9s linear infinite;color:var(--acc)}
@keyframes spin{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}

/* stages */
.stg{scroll-margin-top:120px}
.walk .stg{display:none}
.walk .stg.on{display:block;animation:in .22s var(--ease) both}
.report .stg+.stg{margin-top:56px;padding-top:40px;border-top:1px solid var(--line)}
@keyframes in{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(6px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}
.sh{display:flex;align-items:flex-end;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:18px}
.sh .ey{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);font-weight:500}
.sh h2{font-size:22px;line-height:1.25;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:700;margin-top:4px}
.sh h2:focus{outline:0}
.sh p{color:var(--ink2);font-size:15px;margin-top:6px;max-width:68ch}
.sh .sa{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap}

/* code block */
.cb{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:var(--r);background:var(--panel);overflow:hidden;box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.cb-h{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;min-height:38px;padding:4px 6px 4px 12px;background:var(--sunk);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.cb-h .cn{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;min-width:0;font-weight:500;color:var(--ink2);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
.cb-h .cn .mono{font-size:12px}
.cb-h .sp{flex:1}
.cb-b{overflow-x:auto;padding:8px 0;font:13px/1.7 var(--mono);color:var(--ink)}
.cb-b.tall{max-height:360px;overflow-y:auto}
.ln{display:grid;grid-template-columns:46px minmax(0,1fr);min-width:max-content}
.ln .n{color:var(--faint);text-align:right;padding-right:14px;user-select:none;-webkit-user-select:none}
.ln .t{white-space:pre;padding-right:20px}
.wrapl .ln{min-width:0}
.wrapl .ln .t{white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.ln .t .p{color:var(--faint);user-select:none;-webkit-user-select:none}
.ln.err{background:var(--bad-bg)}
.ln.err .t{color:var(--bad)}
.ln.err .n{color:var(--bad)}
.cb-more{display:flex;justify-content:center;padding:6px;border-top:1px dashed var(--line);background:var(--sunk)}
/* diff */
.dl{display:grid;grid-template-columns:44px 44px 22px minmax(0,1fr);min-width:max-content}
.dl .n{color:var(--faint);text-align:right;padding-right:10px;user-select:none;-webkit-user-select:none}
.dl .g{user-select:none;-webkit-user-select:none;text-align:center;color:var(--faint)}
.dl .t{white-space:pre;padding-right:20px}
.wrapl .dl{min-width:0}.wrapl .dl .t{white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.dl.a{background:var(--ok-bg)}.dl.a .n{background:var(--ok-ln);color:var(--ok)}.dl.a .g{color:var(--ok)}
.dl.d{background:var(--bad-bg)}.dl.d .n{background:var(--bad-ln);color:var(--bad)}.dl.d .g{color:var(--bad)}
.dl.a mark{background:var(--ok-mk);color:inherit;border-radius:3px}
.dl.d mark{background:var(--bad-mk);color:inherit;border-radius:3px}
.dl.hk{background:var(--acc-bg);color:var(--acc-d)}.dl.hk .n{color:var(--acc)}
.dl.nt .t{color:var(--mut)}
.dstat{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font:12px var(--mono)}
.dstat .a{color:var(--ok)}.dstat .d{color:var(--bad)}
.dstat i{display:inline-flex;gap:2px}
.dstat i b{width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--line)}
.dstat i b.a{background:var(--ok)}.dstat i b.d{background:var(--bad)}

/* quote */
.quote{display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto minmax(0,1fr);gap:4px 10px;align-items:start;padding:12px 14px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--sunk);border:1px solid var(--line2);font-size:14.5px;line-height:1.55;color:var(--ink)}
.quote .qk{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut);grid-column:1/-1;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}
.quote blockquote{grid-column:1/-1;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.quote mark{background:var(--bad-bg);color:var(--bad);border-radius:4px;padding:0 3px;font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.92em}

/* read stage */
.browser{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);overflow:hidden;box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.bw-bar{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;height:40px;padding:0 6px 0 12px;background:var(--sunk);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
.bw-bar .dots{display:flex;gap:6px}.bw-bar .dots i{width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--line)}
.bw-url{flex:1;min-width:0;height:26px;border-radius:7px;background:var(--panel);border:1px solid var(--line2);display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:0 9px;font:12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--ink2);overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap}
.bw-url span{overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
.bw-url svg.i{width:13px;height:13px;color:var(--faint)}
.bw-body{padding:22px 22px 24px}
.bw-body h3{font-size:20px;letter-spacing:-.02em;line-height:1.25}
.bw-body .found{margin-top:14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px}
.bw-body .found code{display:block;font-size:12.5px;background:var(--sunk);border:1px solid var(--line2);border-radius:7px;padding:6px 10px;white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;color:var(--ink2)}
.bw-body .found code mark{background:var(--acc-bg);color:var(--acc-d);border-radius:4px;padding:0 5px;margin-right:8px;font-weight:600}
.kv{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));margin-top:16px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel)}
.kv>div{padding:12px 16px;min-width:0}
.kv>div:not(:nth-child(3n+1)){border-left:1px solid var(--line2)}
.kv>div:nth-child(n+4){border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.kv dt{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.kv dd{font-size:14px;font-weight:500;margin-top:2px;overflow-wrap:anywhere}

/* plan */
.plan{list-style:none;padding:0;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh);overflow:hidden}
.plan li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:28px minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:2px 12px;padding:12px 16px;align-items:baseline}
.plan li+li{border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.plan .pn{font:600 12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--mut);text-align:right}
.plan .pi{font-size:14.5px;font-weight:500}
.plan code{grid-column:2;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;display:block}
.plan .pk{font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.plan li.skip .pi{color:var(--mut)}
.plan li.skip .why2{grid-column:2;font-size:13px;color:var(--mut)}

/* run */
.sum{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:14px}
.segs{display:flex;gap:3px;flex:1;min-width:220px}
.segs button{flex:1;height:10px;border:0;border-radius:3px;background:var(--line);cursor:pointer;padding:0;transition:transform .15s var(--ease)}
.segs button:hover{transform:scaleY(1.5)}
.segs button.ok{background:var(--ok)}.segs button.fix{background:var(--warn-dot)}.segs button.bad{background:var(--bad)}.segs button.skip{background:var(--line)}.segs button.run{background:var(--acc)}
.legend{display:flex;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.legend span{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}
.legend i{width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:2px;display:inline-block}
.steps{list-style:none;padding:0;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh);overflow:hidden}
.steps>li+li{border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.st-h{display:grid;grid-template-columns:14px 18px 30px minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:10px;align-items:center;width:100%;padding:11px 14px;border:0;background:none;text-align:left;cursor:pointer}
.st-h:hover{background:var(--hover)}
.st-h:focus-visible{outline-offset:-2px}
.st-h .cv{color:var(--faint);transition:transform .18s var(--ease)}
.st-h[aria-expanded=true] .cv{transform:rotate(90deg)}
.st-h .sn{font:500 12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--mut)}
.st-h .tx{min-width:0}
.st-h .ti{font-size:14.5px;font-weight:500;display:block;white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
.st-h .tc{display:block;font:12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--mut);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;margin-top:1px}
.st-h .mt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font:12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--mut);white-space:nowrap}
.chip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;height:20px;padding:0 7px;border-radius:99px;font:600 11.5px Geist,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif;background:var(--sunk);color:var(--ink2);border:1px solid var(--line2);white-space:nowrap}
.chip.warn{background:var(--warn-bg);color:var(--warn);border-color:transparent}
.chip.bad{background:var(--bad-bg);color:var(--bad);border-color:transparent}
.chip.ok{background:var(--ok-bg);color:var(--ok);border-color:transparent}
.chip.acc{background:var(--acc-bg);color:var(--acc-d);border-color:transparent}
.st-b{padding:2px 16px 18px 86px;display:grid;gap:12px}
.st-b .note{font-size:14px;color:var(--ink2)}
.st-b .note a{font-weight:500}
.st-b .foot2{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center}
.steps>li.live{background:var(--acc-bg)}
.steps>li.q .st-h{opacity:.5}
.steps>li.hl{box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px var(--acc-ln)}
.att{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);font-weight:500}
.att b{font-weight:600;color:var(--ink2)}

/* fix */
.fix+.fix{margin-top:36px;padding-top:32px;border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.fx-h{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.fx-h h3{font-size:17px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.01em;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.fx-g{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 260px;gap:20px;margin-top:14px;align-items:start}
.fx-g>div{min-width:0;display:grid;gap:12px}
.why{font-size:14.5px;color:var(--ink2);line-height:1.6;max-width:72ch}
.why a{font-weight:500}
.cls{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);padding:14px 16px;box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.cls h4{font-size:12.5px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut)}
.bars{display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto;gap:8px 10px;margin-top:10px;align-items:center;font-size:12.5px}
.bars .k{font-family:var(--mono);color:var(--mut)}
.bars .k.top{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}
.bars .v{font-family:var(--mono);color:var(--mut);text-align:right}
.trk{height:6px;border-radius:6px;background:var(--line2);overflow:hidden}
.trk i{display:block;height:100%;width:0;border-radius:6px;background:var(--faint);transition:width .5s var(--ease)}
.trk i.top{background:var(--acc)}
.cls small{display:block;margin-top:10px;color:var(--mut);font-size:12px}
.gave{margin-top:16px;padding:12px 16px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--warn-bg);color:var(--warn);font-size:14px}

/* prove */
.verdict{display:grid;grid-template-columns:48px minmax(0,1fr);gap:4px 16px;align-items:start;padding:22px;border-radius:14px;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.verdict .vi{width:48px;height:48px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;grid-row:span 3}
.verdict .vi svg.i{width:24px;height:24px;stroke-width:2.2}
.verdict.ok .vi{background:var(--ok-bg);color:var(--ok)}
.verdict.bad .vi{background:var(--bad-bg);color:var(--bad)}
.verdict.warn .vi{background:var(--warn-bg);color:var(--warn)}
.verdict h3{font-size:19px;letter-spacing:-.015em;line-height:1.3}
.verdict p{color:var(--ink2);font-size:14.5px;max-width:68ch}
.cells{display:flex;gap:4px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:10px}
.cells i{width:24px;height:24px;border-radius:5px;background:var(--line2);display:grid;place-items:center;font:600 10.5px var(--mono);color:var(--mut);font-style:normal}
.cells i.ok{background:var(--ok-bg);color:var(--ok);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ok-ln)}
.cells i.bad{background:var(--bad-bg);color:var(--bad)}
.pv-why{margin-top:16px;font-size:14px;color:var(--mut);max-width:72ch}

/* graph */
.gtop{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:12px 20px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:14px}
.segc{display:inline-flex;padding:3px;border-radius:9px;background:var(--line2);gap:2px}
.segc button{border:0;background:none;height:28px;padding:0 12px;border-radius:7px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;color:var(--mut);cursor:pointer}
.segc button:hover{color:var(--ink)}
.segc button[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--panel);color:var(--ink);box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.gkey{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px 14px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut)}
.gkey span{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}
.gkey i{width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:50%;display:inline-block}
.gwrap{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 400px;gap:20px;align-items:start}
.gwrap.wide{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}
.gwrap.wide .gpan{display:none}
.gbox{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh);min-width:0}
.graph{list-style:none;padding:14px 12px 14px 16px}
.graph>li{position:relative;padding-left:32px}
.graph>li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:10px;top:0;bottom:0;width:1.5px;background:var(--line)}
.graph>li:first-child::before{top:20px}
.graph>li:last-child::before{bottom:auto;height:20px}
.gb{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:2px 12px;width:100%;padding:9px 12px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:9px;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;position:relative;min-height:44px}
.gb:hover{background:var(--hover)}
.gb[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--acc-bg);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--acc-ln)}
.gd{position:absolute;left:-32px;top:11px;width:20px;height:20px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;color:oklch(99% 0 0);background:var(--faint);box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--panel);font:700 11px var(--mono)}
.gd svg.i{width:12px;height:12px;stroke-width:2.4}
.gs{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut)}
.gc{grid-column:1;font-size:13.5px;overflow-wrap:anywhere;white-space:pre-wrap;color:var(--ink)}
.gc.mono{font-size:12.5px}
.gr{grid-column:2;grid-row:1/3;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:flex-end;justify-content:center;gap:4px}
.gl{font-size:12.5px;font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap}
.n-pass .gd{background:var(--ok)}.n-pass .gl{color:var(--ok)}
.n-docs .gd,.n-fail .gd{background:var(--bad)}.n-docs .gl,.n-fail .gl{color:var(--bad)}
.n-env .gd{background:var(--warn-dot)}.n-env .gl{color:var(--warn)}
.n-block .gd{background:var(--panel);box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--panel),inset 0 0 0 2px var(--warn-dot);color:var(--warn)}.n-block .gl{color:var(--warn)}
.n-none .gd,.n-skip .gd{background:var(--panel);box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--panel),inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--faint);color:var(--mut)}.n-none .gl,.n-skip .gl{color:var(--mut)}
.n-root .gd{background:var(--acc)}.n-end .gd{background:var(--ok)}.n-end .gl{color:var(--ok)}
.n-end.bad .gd{background:var(--warn-dot)}.n-end.bad .gl{color:var(--warn)}
.br{list-style:none;padding:2px 0 10px 12px;margin:0 0 4px 12px;font-size:13px}
.br li{position:relative;padding:5px 0 5px 22px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto minmax(0,1fr);gap:0 10px;align-items:baseline}
.br li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;top:0;bottom:0;width:1.5px;background:var(--line)}
.br li:last-child::before{bottom:50%}
.br li::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;top:50%;width:14px;height:1.5px;background:var(--line)}
.br .bk{color:var(--mut);font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap}
.br .bv{overflow-wrap:anywhere;min-width:0;color:var(--ink2)}
.br .bv.mono{font-size:12.5px}
.br .ok{color:var(--ok);font-weight:600}.br .bad{color:var(--bad);font-weight:600}
.gpan{position:sticky;top:130px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh);padding:18px;max-height:calc(100vh - 150px);overflow:auto;display:grid;gap:10px;align-content:start}
.gpan h3{font-size:16px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-.01em;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.gpan .pk{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut);margin-top:8px}
.gpan .mut{color:var(--mut);font-size:14px}
.gpan ol{padding-left:20px;font-size:14px}
.gpan ol li{margin-top:4px;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.gpan .ok{color:var(--ok);font-weight:600}.gpan .bad{color:var(--bad);font-weight:600}
.evl{list-style:none;padding:0;font-size:14px;display:grid;gap:6px}
.evp{list-style:none;padding:18px 16px 18px 20px}
.evp>li{position:relative;padding:0 0 18px 34px}
.evp>li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:9px;top:0;bottom:0;width:1.5px;background:var(--line)}
.evp>li:first-child::before{top:10px}
.evp>li:last-child::before{bottom:auto;height:10px}
.evp>li:last-child{padding-bottom:0}
.evp .gd{left:0;top:2px;background:var(--acc)}
.evp .ek{display:block;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut)}
.evp .ev{font-size:14.5px;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.evp .es{display:block;font-size:13px;color:var(--mut);margin-top:2px}
.lg2{display:inline-block;margin-left:6px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:99px;padding:0 7px;vertical-align:1px}

/* bisect */
.tl{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh);padding:26px 20px 18px;overflow-x:auto}
.tlr{display:flex;position:relative;min-width:max-content}
.tlr::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:36px;right:36px;top:31px;height:2px;background:var(--line)}
.rel{position:relative;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:5px;min-width:96px;flex:1;font-size:12px;color:var(--mut)}
.rel .tg{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;color:var(--bad);min-height:15px;letter-spacing:.02em}
.rel i{width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--faint);box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--panel);position:relative}
.rel.p i{background:var(--ok)}.rel.f i{background:var(--bad)}
.rel.first i{box-shadow:0 0 0 4px var(--panel),0 0 0 7px var(--bad-ln)}
.rel b{font:600 12.5px var(--mono);color:var(--ink)}
.rel.first b{color:var(--bad)}
.rel.anim{opacity:.25;transition:opacity .3s var(--ease)}
.rel.anim.on{opacity:1}
.nt-row{margin-top:16px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--mut);display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.nt-row i{width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--line);display:inline-block}
.tblw{overflow-x:auto;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:var(--sh)}
.tbl{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:13.5px}
.tbl th{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--mut);text-align:left;padding:9px 14px;background:var(--sunk);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);white-space:nowrap}
.tbl td{padding:10px 14px;border-top:1px solid var(--line2);vertical-align:top;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.tbl tr:first-child td{border-top:0}
.tbl td.mono{font-size:12.5px}
.tbl .res{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font-weight:500;white-space:nowrap}
.tbl tr.first td{background:var(--bad-bg)}
.call{margin-top:14px;padding:14px 16px;border-radius:12px;background:var(--sunk);border:1px solid var(--line2);font-size:14.5px}
.call b{font-weight:600}
.call small{display:block;color:var(--mut);font-size:13px;margin-top:3px}
.mt16{margin-top:16px}
.mt12{margin-top:12px}

/* prereqs */
.pq-st{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;margin-top:14px;font-size:14.5px;font-weight:500}
.pq-st small{display:block;color:var(--mut);font-weight:400;font-size:13px;margin-top:2px}

/* footer */
.foot{border-top:1px solid var(--line);margin-top:8px;background:var(--panel)}
.foot-in{max-width:1280px;margin:0 auto;padding:28px 20px 36px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) auto;gap:20px 40px;align-items:end}
.foot h2{font-size:15px;font-weight:600}
.foot p{color:var(--mut);font-size:13.5px;margin-top:2px}
.cmdbox{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin-top:12px;max-width:620px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;background:var(--sunk);padding:6px 6px 6px 14px}
.cmdbox code{flex:1;min-width:0;overflow-x:auto;white-space:nowrap;font-size:13.5px;padding:4px 0}
.cmdbox .p{color:var(--faint)}
.foot nav{display:flex;gap:18px;font-size:13.5px;flex-wrap:wrap}
.foot nav a{color:var(--mut);text-decoration:none}
.foot nav a:hover{color:var(--ink)}

/* pager */
.pager{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;margin-top:32px;padding-top:20px;border-top:1px solid var(--line)}
.pager .pd{display:flex;gap:6px}
.pager .pd button{width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;border:0;padding:0;background:var(--line);cursor:pointer;transition:background .15s,width .2s var(--ease)}
.pager .pd button[aria-current=step]{background:var(--ink);width:20px;border-radius:4px}
.pager .pv,.pager .nx{min-width:0}
.pager .b span.lb{max-width:24ch;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
.report .pager{display:none}

/* keyboard help */
.keys{display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr;gap:8px 14px;padding:8px 10px 10px;font-size:13.5px;color:var(--ink2);align-items:center}
.keys>span{display:flex;gap:4px}

@media (max-width:1100px){.gwrap{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}.gpan{position:static;max-height:none}}
@media (max-width:1000px){
.shell{grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:16px;padding-top:0}
.rail{position:sticky;top:98px;z-index:20;background:var(--bg);margin:0 -20px;padding:8px 20px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
.rail h2,.rail .meter{display:none}
.rail ol{display:flex;gap:6px;overflow-x:auto;scrollbar-width:none}
.rail ol::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}
.rail li+li::before{display:none}
.rb{grid-template-columns:auto auto;white-space:nowrap;padding:6px 10px;gap:0 7px}
.rb .rs{display:none}
.rb svg.i{width:16px;height:16px;background:none}
.stg{scroll-margin-top:160px}
html{scroll-padding-top:170px}
.fx-g{grid-template-columns:1fr}
.facts{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
.facts>div:nth-child(odd){border-left:0}
.facts>div:nth-child(n+3){border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.gpan{top:170px}
}
@media (max-width:640px){
.top-in{padding:0 12px;gap:6px}
.crumbs .sl,.crumbs .now,.crumbs a{display:none}
.top .hide-s{display:none}
.wrap{padding:0 16px}
.rail{margin:0 -16px;padding:8px 16px}
.rh h1{font-size:23px}
.rh-acts{width:100%}
.tabs .hint{display:none}
.st-h{grid-template-columns:12px 18px minmax(0,1fr);padding:10px 12px;gap:8px}
.st-h .sn{display:none}
.st-h .mt{grid-column:3;justify-self:start}
.st-b{padding:2px 12px 14px}
.kv{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}
.kv>div{border-left:0!important;border-top:1px solid var(--line2)}
.kv>div:nth-child(-n+2){border-top:0}
.kv>div:nth-child(even){border-left:1px solid var(--line2)!important}
.verdict{grid-template-columns:1fr;padding:18px}
.verdict .vi{grid-row:auto}
.foot-in{grid-template-columns:1fr;padding:24px 16px 32px}
.pager .b span.lb{max-width:11ch}
.intro{padding:36px 16px 48px}
.intro h1{font-size:27px}
.gal button{grid-template-columns:18px minmax(0,1fr)}
.gal .gm{grid-column:2}
.dl{grid-template-columns:34px 34px 18px minmax(0,1fr)}
.ln{grid-template-columns:36px minmax(0,1fr)}
.cmdbox{flex-wrap:wrap}
.gb{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}
.gr{grid-column:1;grid-row:auto;flex-direction:row;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;justify-content:flex-start}
.br{margin-left:4px;padding-left:6px}.br li{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);padding-left:18px}.br li::after{top:14px;width:10px}
.graph{padding:12px 8px 12px 12px}
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*,*::before,*::after{animation-duration:.01ms!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important;transition-duration:.01ms!important}}
</style>

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

- Run steps are log rows. Each row shows the docs quote with the failing command marked, every attempt with its exit code, and line-numbered output with wrap and copy.
- Fixes and the PR show unified diffs with line numbers and word-level marks.

input.description: Demo video inspiration sheet
input.prompt:
Prepare a demo-video inspiration and shot sheet for FirstRun, Atharva Shah's neatHack 2026 hackathon project. Do NOT create any video, do not render anything, do not commit or push. Another Claude session may be editing the vault, so only create your one new file.

## Goal
A spectacular, "million-dollar" product demo under 2 minutes that combines three footage types: (1) human footage Atharva shoots on a DJI Action 4 camera, (2) screen recordings, (3) demo/motion elements. The app may change a lot by tomorrow, so the sheet must be modular: shots grouped by story beat, each marked "stable" (won't change) or "re-shoot if UI changes".

## Read first
- Atharva's global writing rules apply to all prose: no em/en dashes, no semicolons, sentences of 20 words or fewer, active voice, commands for actions, numbered lists only for sequences.
- D:\Atharva\NOTES\CLAUDE.md for where a file like this belongs in the vault and its frontmatter conventions. If a video/demo folder exists in NOTES, use it. Otherwise save to D:\Atharva\NOTES\ in the folder the vault rules suggest for project planning.
- The skills C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.claude\skills\video-make\SKILL.md, C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.claude\skills\video-edit\SKILL.md and C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.claude\skills\product-launch-video (if present) for what the toolchain can do later (HyperFrames motion graphics, captions, cuts), so the plan matches real capabilities. Read only.
- Product facts (read, do not invent): D:\Atharva\firstrun\README.md, D:\Atharva\firstrun\hackathon.md (build log), D:\Atharva\firstrun\docs\index.html (landing page copy and its 44-second launch film at docs/assets/firstrun-launch.mp4), and the worktree D:\Atharva\firstrun-run\docs\run.html (the new /run replay page: GitHub-Actions-style run view, walkthrough stages Read, Plan, Run, Fix, Prove, Docs graph, When did it break?, What the docs assume, Pull request; share popover; downloads; ?s=10#ex=dbt deep link to the dbt step 10 failure). Live: https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/ and https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html#ex=dbt
- Core story facts: FirstRun runs a docs quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, fixes it, and proves the fix with a second clean run. Real wins: dbt guide `jafgen --years 6` broke in jafgen 0.4.6 (2024-04-07), fix proven 9/9 in a fresh container, upstream PRs dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10149 and #10150, entireio/cli#2724. Sponsor tools: neatlogs (tracing), Entire (session capture), cfo.ai (business plan), Jev/TypeSafe (classifier), Firecrawl, Claude Agent SDK.

## Sheet contents
1. One-line hook and the 2-minute story spine as timed beats (for example 0:00 to 0:08 cold open...). Total under 2:00.
2. B-roll list for the DJI Action 4: each shot with framing, mount/angle (chest mount, desk clamp, low-angle, POV over shoulder, timelapse), lens mode, frame rate (e.g. 4K 60 or 120 for slow-mo), lighting note, duration, and which beat it serves. Include human moments (frustration at broken docs, the "it passed" reaction, typing, coffee/night timelapse, phone notification of the PR).
3. Screen captures list: exact URL or command, viewport size (1920x1080 and a 1080x1920 vertical variant), what to click, cursor guidance, zoom/crop target, and stable vs re-shoot flag. Cover terminal `firstrun <url>` run, the /run walkthrough stages, the share popover, the GitHub PR pages, neatlogs trace, Entire session, the landing page.
4. Other visual elements: motion-graphic title cards, kinetic text callouts, number reveals (9/9, 10m to first success, $0.03), diff animations, logo lockups for sponsors, captions style, music mood and BPM, sound design (keyboard, success chime), transitions, color/LUT notes matching the site's light Apple-style look.
5. Shot checklist table ready to tick off on shoot day, plus a gear and settings checklist for the DJI Action 4.
6. Three reference demos for inspiration (real, well-known product launch videos, e.g. Linear, Vercel, Arc, Apple) with one line each on what to borrow. Only cite ones you are confident exist.

Report back the absolute file path and a 5-line summary of the story spine.

content.content:
1	---
2	type: Identity Profile
3	title: "Runtime Contract"
4	description: "The load order for every writing job, and the checks that run after."
5	created: 2026-08-22
6	updated: 2026-09-25
7	---
8	
9	# Runtime Contract
10	
11	> **Purpose:** This file says which rules load, in what order, and which checks run at the end.
12	> It is the only file that answers "what was applied to this draft". Read it first, every time.
13	> Adapted from the runtime contract in [Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer](https://github.com/Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer).
14	> The architecture is theirs. The rules and the voice are mine.
15	
16	## Always loaded
17	
18	Six files load for every piece of writing, on every channel, in this order.
19	
20	1. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, this file. The load order and the checks.
21	2. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`. The failure patterns a regex cannot see.
22	3. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/write-simply.md`. The plain style, and the test for whether the ideas are right.
23	4. `DIGITAL TWIN/World.md`. The villain, the vision, and what the piece is for.
24	5. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. The bar the insight clears before a word is drafted.
25	6. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`. How the writing sounds.
26	
27	Files 2 and 3 are a pair. The pattern rules say what to remove, and `write-simply.md` says what to
28	aim for, so a draft that only obeys the first one reads stripped.
29	
30	`World.md` decides what the piece argues and `Voice.md` decides how it sounds, so the two never
31	collide. Name the skill-tree node before you draft a line. A piece that advances no node is an
32	idea, so send it back to `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS/`.
33	
34	`net-new-value.md` is the guiding principle for all content, on every channel. Write the core
35	insight as one sentence and name its box before you draft. Only box 4 ships: non-obvious to the
36	reader and tactical enough to use today. A piece outside box 4 gets one upgrade, then goes back to
37	the idea bank.
38	
39	`SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` holds the banned words, phrases and punctuation. `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/`
40	holds the prose rules, one file each. The `core` rules load into every session through the generated
41	block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so you never copy them into another file.
42	
43	The `craft` rules load for every writing job. Run this once per session before the first draft:
44	
45	```bash
46	python SCRIPTS/slop/rules_prompt.py --profile craft
47	```
48	
49	## Loaded on demand
50	
51	One more file loads, chosen by the job. Never load two.
52	
53	| The job | Load this |
54	|---|---|
55	| A Substack article, an essay, a long piece | `DIGITAL TWIN/Long-Form Writing Rules.md` |
56	| A tutorial, a how-to, a README, developer docs | `DIGITAL TWIN/Technical Writing Style Guide.md` |
57	| A LinkedIn post, a Note, a tweet, a caption | nothing extra. The channel skill carries it |
58	
59	`DIGITAL TWIN/AI Writing Policy.md` outranks all of the above and it changes rarely, so read it
60	when you start a writing session and not once per draft.
61	
62	## Then the channel skill
63	
64	The skill carries the shape of the channel and nothing else. It never restates a banned word, a
65	voice rule or a craft rule, because a copy goes stale and then two files disagree.
66	
67	| Channel | Skill |
68	|---|---|
69	| LinkedIn post | `.claude/skills/write-linkedin-posts/SKILL.md` |
70	| X post or thread | `.claude/skills/banger-tweets/SKILL.md` |
71	| Substack Note | `.claude/skills/substack-notes/SKILL.md` |
72	| Substack article | `.claude/skills/substack-writer/SKILL.md` |
73	| Reddit post | none. `SOCIALS/Reddit/README.md` is the channel spec |
74	| Landing page or sales email | `.claude/skills/write-sales-copy/SKILL.md` |
75	| A stuck idea with no shape yet | `.claude/skills/write-outline/SKILL.md` |
76	| An existing draft that reads like AI | `.claude/skills/deslop-audit/SKILL.md` |
77	
78	## Precedence, higher wins
79	
80	Four layers can disagree. Resolve upward.
81	
82	1. The banned lists in `slop_rules.py` and the patterns in `core/pattern-rules.md`.
83	2. The channel skill.
84	3. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`.
85	4. A sample Atharva pastes in the current session.
86	
87	A sample beats the profile. The profile beats the skill. Two rules never override anything above
88	them. The fabrication rule below, and the five principles in `AI Writing Policy.md`.
89	
90	## The fabrication rule
91	
92	Add no fact that Atharva did not supply. That covers a name, a number, a date, a statistic, a
93	quote, a source, an event and a client. This rule bites hardest on a rewrite, because the fix for
94	a vague sentence looks like a specific sentence, and the specifics are not yours to invent.
95	
96	You have three legal moves when a sentence needs a real detail.
97	
98	1. Ask him for it.
99	2. Mark the gap in visible brackets, such as `[the real number]`. Brackets cannot ship by accident.
100	3. Drop the claim to the level the evidence supports, or cut it.
101	
102	An invented specific that reads well is a worse defect than the vague sentence it replaced. A
103	reader cannot catch it.
104	
105	## The two-pass loop
106	
107	Never hand over a first draft.
108	
109	**Pass 1.** Write it. Do not judge while you write.
110	
111	**Pass 2.** Read it cold and answer five questions for yourself, in writing. Do not print the
112	answers unless he asks.
113	
114	1. If a reader called this AI, which exact sentence would they point at?
115	2. Does the draft carry a fact, a name, a number or a source that he did not give me?
116	3. Which sentence is the weakest, and does the piece rest on it?
117	4. Which sentence reads worst, and is the idea under it wrong rather than the wording?
118	5. Is the core insight still box 4 in `core/net-new-value.md`, or did the draft sand it down to box 2?
119	
120	**Pass 3.** Fix what the answers found. Then run the checks.
121	
122	## Announce the load order
123	
124	Render this panel above every draft. Do not type it by hand.
125	
126	```bash
127	python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill <channel skill> --file "<path>"     --node "<the skill-tree node this piece advances>"     --topic "<the idea, for the pillar check>"     --season "<NN beat N, or none>" --format "<number and name, or n/a>"     --insight "<the box 4 insight, one sentence>"
128	```
129	
130	`--glob "<pattern>"` replaces `--file` for a batch, and reports the worst result
131	across the set. `--plain` drops to ASCII. `--technical` swaps the on-demand file
132	for the Technical Writing Style Guide. The script exits 1 when any measured check
133	failed, so a caller can gate on it.

type: Identity Profile
title: "Runtime Contract"
description: "The load order for every writing job, and the checks that run after."
created: 2026-08-22
updated: 2026-09-25

# Runtime Contract

> **Purpose:** This file says which rules load, in what order, and which checks run at the end.
> It is the only file that answers "what was applied to this draft". Read it first, every time.
> Adapted from the runtime contract in [Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer](https://github.com/Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer).
> The architecture is theirs. The rules and the voice are mine.

## Always loaded

Six files load for every piece of writing, on every channel, in this order.

1. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, this file. The load order and the checks.
2. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`. The failure patterns a regex cannot see.
3. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/write-simply.md`. The plain style, and the test for whether the ideas are right.
4. `DIGITAL TWIN/World.md`. The villain, the vision, and what the piece is for.
5. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. The bar the insight clears before a word is drafted.
6. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`. How the writing sounds.

Files 2 and 3 are a pair. The pattern rules say what to remove, and `write-simply.md` says what to
aim for, so a draft that only obeys the first one reads stripped.

`World.md` decides what the piece argues and `Voice.md` decides how it sounds, so the two never
collide. Name the skill-tree node before you draft a line. A piece that advances no node is an
idea, so send it back to `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS/`.

`net-new-value.md` is the guiding principle for all content, on every channel. Write the core
insight as one sentence and name its box before you draft. Only box 4 ships: non-obvious to the
reader and tactical enough to use today. A piece outside box 4 gets one upgrade, then goes back to
the idea bank.

`SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` holds the banned words, phrases and punctuation. `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/`
holds the prose rules, one file each. The `core` rules load into every session through the generated
block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so you never copy them into another file.

The `craft` rules load for every writing job. Run this once per session before the first draft:

```bash
python SCRIPTS/slop/rules_prompt.py --profile craft
```

## Loaded on demand

One more file loads, chosen by the job. Never load two.

| The job | Load this |
|---|---|
| A Substack article, an essay, a long piece | `DIGITAL TWIN/Long-Form Writing Rules.md` |
| A tutorial, a how-to, a README, developer docs | `DIGITAL TWIN/Technical Writing Style Guide.md` |
| A LinkedIn post, a Note, a tweet, a caption | nothing extra. The channel skill carries it |

`DIGITAL TWIN/AI Writing Policy.md` outranks all of the above and it changes rarely, so read it
when you start a writing session and not once per draft.

## Then the channel skill

The skill carries the shape of the channel and nothing else. It never restates a banned word, a
voice rule or a craft rule, because a copy goes stale and then two files disagree.

| Channel | Skill |
|---|---|
| LinkedIn post | `.claude/skills/write-linkedin-posts/SKILL.md` |
| X post or thread | `.claude/skills/banger-tweets/SKILL.md` |
| Substack Note | `.claude/skills/substack-notes/SKILL.md` |
| Substack article | `.claude/skills/substack-writer/SKILL.md` |
| Reddit post | none. `SOCIALS/Reddit/README.md` is the channel spec |
| Landing page or sales email | `.claude/skills/write-sales-copy/SKILL.md` |
| A stuck idea with no shape yet | `.claude/skills/write-outline/SKILL.md` |
| An existing draft that reads like AI | `.claude/skills/deslop-audit/SKILL.md` |

## Precedence, higher wins

Four layers can disagree. Resolve upward.

1. The banned lists in `slop_rules.py` and the patterns in `core/pattern-rules.md`.
2. The channel skill.
3. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`.
4. A sample Atharva pastes in the current session.

A sample beats the profile. The profile beats the skill. Two rules never override anything above
them. The fabrication rule below, and the five principles in `AI Writing Policy.md`.

## The fabrication rule

Add no fact that Atharva did not supply. That covers a name, a number, a date, a statistic, a
quote, a source, an event and a client. This rule bites hardest on a rewrite, because the fix for
a vague sentence looks like a specific sentence, and the specifics are not yours to invent.

You have three legal moves when a sentence needs a real detail.

1. Ask him for it.
2. Mark the gap in visible brackets, such as `[the real number]`. Brackets cannot ship by accident.
3. Drop the claim to the level the evidence supports, or cut it.

An invented specific that reads well is a worse defect than the vague sentence it replaced. A
reader cannot catch it.

## The two-pass loop

Never hand over a first draft.

**Pass 1.** Write it. Do not judge while you write.

**Pass 2.** Read it cold and answer five questions for yourself, in writing. Do not print the
answers unless he asks.

1. If a reader called this AI, which exact sentence would they point at?
2. Does the draft carry a fact, a name, a number or a source that he did not give me?
3. Which sentence is the weakest, and does the piece rest on it?
4. Which sentence reads worst, and is the idea under it wrong rather than the wording?
5. Is the core insight still box 4 in `core/net-new-value.md`, or did the draft sand it down to box 2?

**Pass 3.** Fix what the answers found. Then run the checks.

## Announce the load order

Render this panel above every draft. Do not type it by hand.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill <channel skill> --file "<path>"     --node "<the skill-tree node this piece advances>"     --topic "<the idea, for the pillar check>"     --season "<NN beat N, or none>" --format "<number and name, or n/a>"     --insight "<the box 4 insight, one sentence>"
```

`--glob "<pattern>"` replaces `--file` for a batch, and reports the worst result
across the set. `--plain` drops to ASCII. `--technical` swaps the on-demand file
for the Technical Writing Style Guide. The script exits 1 when any measured check
failed, so a caller can gate on it.

```
╭─ LOAD ORDER ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ✓ 1  core/runtime-contract              always               │
│ ✓ 2  core/pattern-rules                 always               │
│ ✓ 3  core/write-simply                  always               │
│ ✓ 4  World.md                           always               │
│ ✓ 5  core/net-new-value                 always               │
│ ✓ 6  Voice.md                           always               │
│ ✓ 7  Long-Form Writing Rules.md         on demand            │
│ ✓ 8  skill:substack-writer              channel              │
├─ WORLD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ villain  rented work                                         │
│ node     builds a gate that refuses bad work                 │
│ season   01 beat 3      format  05 Contrarian Take           │
│ insight  a hook that returns decision: block stops the save  │
├─ CHECKS, measured ───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✓ pillar      ON (AI)                                        │
│ ✓ slop        CRIT 0                                         │
│ ✓ clarity     CRIT 0                                         │
│ ✓ craft       0                                              │
│ ✓ seo         CRIT 0                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The two halves carry different weight, and the difference is the point.

**The top half is declared.** You state the node, the season and the box 4 insight. The chain itself
comes from the channel table inside the script, so it cannot drift from this file.

**The bottom half is measured.** The script runs each scorer and prints what it
returned. A tick means a check ran and passed. A cross means it ran and failed. A
dot means the scorer could not run, which never reads as a pass.

That split is why the panel replaced the four hand-typed lines it used to be. A
typed line could claim `slop CRIT 0` for a check nobody ran, which is the blind
spot this contract exists to close. A rendered line cannot.

A missing panel means the chain was skipped.

## The checks, in this order

Run them in order. A later check on a draft that fails an earlier one wastes both your time and his.

| Order | Command | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Name the box in `core/net-new-value.md` for the one-sentence insight | Box 4. Every channel |
| 0b | The opening gate in `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md` | The top-ranked of 5 openings ships, and no hook is a question. LinkedIn, X, Notes |
| 1 | `python SCRIPTS/pillars/pillars.py --text "<the idea>"` | ON, or an honest BEND |
| 2 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/overlap.py check "<the idea>"` | WRITE. Articles only |
| 3 | `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0 |
| 4 | `python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. Every channel |
| 5 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. LinkedIn only |
| 6 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/craft.py "<file>"` | 0. Articles only |
| 7 | `python SCRIPTS/seo/score.py "<file>" --write` | 0. Articles only |
| 8 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py` | no `source_blog` warning. Social files only |
| 9 | `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py` | the desk carries it. Every draft is on it, nothing to stamp |

Rows 4, 5 and 6 were missing from this table until 2026-09-04. All three existed
and two of them already blocked a commit, so the table was the only place that
disagreed. A check absent from this file gets skipped by anyone who trusts it,
which is the whole reason the file exists. Add a row here in the same commit
that adds a scorer.

Checks 0, 0b, 1 and 2 run before you draft. Checks 3 to 9 run after. Skip a row only when the row says
so, and say in the announcement block which rows you skipped.

MED and LOW findings from the scorer are advisory. On short-form, ignore its flow, paragraph and
fragment findings, because those rules were written for long-form.

## Related

- [AI Writing Policy](../AI%20Writing%20Policy.md), the top directive, above this file
- [Pattern rules](./pattern-rules.md), the second always-loaded file
- [Write Simply](./write-simply.md), the third always-loaded file, the plain style and its test
- [World](../World.md), the villain, the vision and the skill tree

content.content:
The first post in the file publishes immediately. Every post after it takes the next free slot, three per day, at 10:00, 14:30 and 19:30 IST. The first slot used is the next one still in the future, so a run started at 01:00 fills today and a run started at 20:00 starts tomorrow.

Dry run is the default on every command. Nothing leaves the machine without `--live`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `plan <file>` | Print the schedule, character counts and image flags. Sends nothing. |
| `send <file> --live` | Publish post 1 now, schedule the rest, append to `_sent.tsv`. |
| `sync-media <file> --live` | Attach images to posts that are **already scheduled**, matched on exact text. |
| `list` | Print the whole Zernio queue with status, time and image flag. |
| `publish <post_id> --live` | Send a scheduled post right now instead of waiting for its slot. |
| `cancel <post_id> --live` | Delete one scheduled post. |
| `schedule <file> --at "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" [--every N]` | Schedule at a time you pick, stepping N days per post. Publishes nothing now. |
| `respace --pin <id,id,...>` | Re-space the whole queue onto the slot grid, order kept. Pinned ids hold their time. |

`publish` refuses anything that is not currently scheduled, so it cannot double-post something already live. Publishing early leaves its old slot empty and moves nothing else, so the rest of the queue keeps the times it was given.

Add `--platform youtube` to target another account. The default is `twitter`.

## Picking the time yourself, and fixing an overbooked queue

`send` always publishes post 1 immediately and drops the rest into the next free grid slots. That
is wrong for a post that has to land in one specific slot, so `schedule` takes the time from you.

python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py schedule "SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_Foo.md" --at "2026-08-30 19:30" --live

content.content:
# FirstRun Business Plan

FirstRun runs a dev tool's quickstart in a clean container every night, finds the first step that breaks, proves the fix with a second clean run, and drafts the docs PR. The buyer is a DevRel or docs team at a dev-tool company.

The business plan sets the agent's spending limit. `firstrun econ` reads every neatlogs trace, cfo.ai turns the costs into a per-tier cap, and `firstrun run --tier` stops any run that spends past it.

cfo.ai model, public and read-only: [https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE](https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE)

## Three Tiers Price by Quickstarts Covered

| Tier | Price per month | Quickstarts | Runs per month |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 1, weekly | 4 |
| Team | $49 | 10, nightly | 300 |
| Scale | $299 | 100, nightly, with PRs, Docs Bisect and Prerequisite Proof | 3,000 |

## The Average Run Costs $0.0167, but One in Twenty Costs Three Times That

neatlogs holds 64 `firstrun.run` traces from 2026-10-10. `firstrun econ` reads them and writes [`drivers.csv`](drivers.csv), the file cfo.ai imports. Each quantile row names the trace it came from, so a judge can open the trace behind any cost in the model.

| Driver | Cost per run | neatlogs trace |
|---|---|---|
| Mean | $0.01672 | all 64 |
| p50 | $0.01076 | `cef9cc00bcc5369d74ffc7fc5f525244` |
| p90 | $0.04424 | `ec246a27f83c9e11d682eb09a1818f58` |
| p95 | $0.05078 | `9e30cd0f9cee66410c81fb3a34e03177` |
| Max | $0.10135 | `a462576e751e91543b5623185331d603` |
| Compute | $0.0019 | assumption: AWS t3.medium at $0.0416 an hour for the measured 164.8 s mean |

The costs are Sonnet 5.5 list price, and Anthropic did not bill them. The 64 traces include 28 development runs, so the spread is wider than a production month would show.

The expensive runs are the useful ones. A run that hits a broken step pays for recovery and for the second clean run. Of 19 real-world runs, 10 ended `verified` with 32 proven patches, and the 19 runs cost $0.97 in total. That is $0.0975 per verified quickstart (source: `runs/*/state.json`).

## The Old $0.50 Cap Let a Scale Customer Cost Five Times the Price

Before this plan, every run had the same cap of $0.50 in `src/firstrun/models.py`. That cap was 30 times the mean run cost, and nothing in the business set it.

| Tier | Revenue per run | Margin at mean cost | Margin at p95 cost | Margin if every run hits $0.50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Team | $0.1633 | 88.6% | 67.7% | -207.3% |
| Scale | $0.0997 | 81.3% | 47.1% | -403.6% |

The mean says both tiers are healthy. The p95 says Scale falls below a 70% margin in a month with many broken quickstarts. The old cap says one bad month can cost a Scale customer's fee five times over.

## The Margin Floor Sets the Cap, and the Agent Enforces It

The founder picks one number, a 70% gross margin floor. The cap for each tier is the model spend one run may use and still keep that floor:

```text
cap per run = price / runs per month x (1 - margin floor) - compute per run
```

If every run in a month hits the cap, the tier still earns 70%. A Free run has no revenue, so its cap is the measured median run.

| Tier | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0.0108 | 48.4% |
| Team | $0.0471 | 7.8% |
| Scale | $0.0280 | 25.0% |

## The Planner Fix From the Traces Cut Cost per Run by 24%

neatlogs Detections and an Investigate run found the planner inventing steps. The fix shipped in commit 3ca6f11. The same 4 targets, before and after, as neatlogs measured them:

| Agent | Model cost per run | Quickstarts finished | Failed steps recovered |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | $0.0262 | 2 of 4 | 0 |
| v2 | $0.0200 | 3 of 4 | 3 |

## cfo.ai Shows the Old Cap Runs Out of Cash in Month 14

Ari built the model in cfo.ai over MCP, in workspace "Atharva CFOAI", page "FirstRun model". Every formula reads its number from a "FirstRun drivers" table, and its "Driver source" column names the neatlogs trace behind each measured cost. The figures below were read back from cfo.ai, not computed by hand. Cost per run is $0.01862, the 64-trace mean plus compute. Gross margin includes Stripe fees.
41:| 1:00 to 2:00 | Office hour with Chetan Raj, booked 2026-10-09. Bring a real trace, the title card and the README. | His answers saved in `hackathon.md` | Ask the 3 questions in Discord instead |

## Five Mentors, and the One Question for Each

**Booked: Chetan Raj (2026-10-09).** Use him for packaging, because he is a frontend architect who builds and tests consumer agents. Ask him three things:

1. "Where does a judge stop trusting a demo?" Show 30 seconds of a real run, from the terminal to the trace.
2. "FirstRun has no web UI. Is the terminal plus the report plus neatlogs enough, or does one static HTML report page make the result clearer?" Add the page only if he says yes and Layer 2 is done.
3. "Does the README sell it in 10 seconds?"

Bring a real trace, `META/Attachments/neathack/brand/title-card-1920x1080.jpg` and the README. Rohan Mukherjee was the first pick for the verification question. Ask him in Discord instead.

| Mentor | Who | Ask this in office hours | Links |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rohan Mukherjee | Proximal (RL environments and evals for coding agents, $15M seed). Ex-Dyte founding engineer, ex-Cloudflare AI Gateway. | "How do I stop FirstRun from gaming its own verification run?" | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roerohan/) · [X](https://x.com/roerohan) |
| Ankush Dharkar | Founder of TrueHuman.id and Real Dev Squad. 28.8K X followers, the largest audience of the ten. | "What is the smallest human-in-the-loop check that makes an agent trustworthy?" Also: "What makes a dev audience share a build post?" | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ankushdharkar/) · [X](https://x.com/ankushdharkar) |
| Rithvik K | ML engineer, Palantir SWE, research grantee at Adoption AI. | "How should state survive a crash halfway through a long run?" | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rithvik1709/) · [X](https://x.com/BngRithvik) |
| Karan Pargal | Claims 16+ hackathon wins. Web3 and trading systems. His own profiles still say Covalent/Trench, not Confido Health. | "What do the first 30 seconds of a winning demo video show?" | [LinkedIn](https://in.linkedin.com/in/karan-pargal) · [X](https://x.com/karan_pargal) |

Before this plan, every run had the same cap of $0.50 in `src/firstrun/models.py`. That cap was 30 times the mean run cost, and nothing in the business set it.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Team | $0.1633 | 88.6% | 67.7% | -207.3% |
| Scale | $0.0997 | 81.3% | 47.1% | -403.6% |

The founder picks one number, a 70% gross margin floor. The cap for each tier is the model spend one run may use and still keep that floor:

```text
cap per run = price / runs per month x (1 - margin floor) - compute per run
```

If every run in a month hits the cap, the tier still earns 70%. A Free run has no revenue, so its cap is the measured median run.

| Tier | Cap per run | Measured runs over the cap |

| Free | $0.0108 | 48.4% |
| Team | $0.0471 | 7.8% |
| Scale | $0.0280 | 25.0% |

neatlogs Detections and an Investigate run found the planner inventing steps. The fix shipped in commit 3ca6f11. The same 4 targets, before and after, as neatlogs measured them:

23	   through `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The shapes a regex cannot catch live in `core/pattern-rules.md`.

26	
27	| # | Take (what he believes) | Box (net new value) | Shape | Evidence backing it |
28	|---|---|---|---|---|
29	
30	Never skip the table. It is the difference between drafting and reporting.

32	## When a tweet will not start, borrow a winning shape
33	
34	[Swipefile](https://swipefile.com/) holds about 14,000 tagged examples that already worked, including 903 social and X posts, 3,214 copywriting entries and 2,433 advice entries. Each one carries a short teardown of why it worked. Use [swipefile.com/category/social](https://swipefile.com/category/social) for X specifically.
35	
36	Borrow the shape, never the words. The take stays Atharva's and the evidence stays his. A swiped hook with his claim under it is a tweet. A swiped hook with a swiped claim is theft and it reads like someone else.
37	
38	Read the full entry in `LIBRARY/Lists/tools and software directory.md`.
39	
40	## The one rule that fixes 90% of bad tweets
41	
42	**The claim leads. The evidence backs it up.**
43	
44	A tweet that opens by naming a company, a study, a person, or a report has already failed, because the subject of the sentence becomes "someone did research" instead of "here is what is true".
45	
46	Mechanical test, run it on every draft: **read only the first six words.** If those words name a source, rewrite so the first six words say what you believe.
47	
48	```
49	broken:  SparkToro measured their own accounts and found posts with links reach 10x fewer people.
50	fixed:   a post with a link reaches 10x fewer people than the same post without one. meta wrote
51	         that advice into their own help docs. they're not hiding the toll booth. you keep paying it.
52	```
53	
54	Same fact. The first is a press release. The second costs the reader something.
55	
56	When you are handed raw material (an article, a blog, a situation), find the sharpest uncomfortable truth inside it. That single sentence is the tweet. Everything else is packaging.
57	
58	> **Where the angle comes from.** Pick the subject and argument shape from `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Content Formats - 100 Post Ideas.md`, top 10 first. That file never chooses the wording. Everything below governs how the tweet reads, and a tweet that sounds like a LinkedIn post has failed no matter which format it came from.
59	
60	## No links in the post
61	
62	An X post carries no URL. Not to the blog, not to a repository, not to a tool. X cuts the reach of a post that sends the reader off the platform, and Atharva pays that toll on every scheduled post.
63	
64	This binds hardest on anything going out through Zernio, because those post on a schedule with nobody watching the numbers. Write the post so it stands alone and pays the reader on X.
65	
66	Three ways to keep the value without the link.
67	
68	**Name the thing.** "the glossary" and "pocketflow" cost nothing and a reader who wants it can search.
69	
70	**Give the substance away.** The post carries the number, the rule or the step. A reader who wants the rest goes looking without being told to.
71	
72	**End on the claim.** A post that ends on a URL taught the reader that the post was an advertisement. End on the sentence that was worth reading.
73	
74	Never replace a link with "link in bio", "link in the replies", or "DM me for it". Those are the same toll with extra steps.
75	
76	## One post, never a thread
77	
78	Atharva is on X Premium+. One post holds up to 25,000 characters, so the reason threads existed is gone. Three rules follow from that and none of them bends.
79	
80	**Never number a post.** No `1/`, no `2/`, no `🧵`, no "a thread". A point that needed three numbered parts is one post that runs longer.
81	
82	**Never write a pinned comment.** The pinned first comment is a LinkedIn mechanic and it belongs to `write-linkedin-posts` alone. On X the link goes in the post body.
83	
84	**Never split one argument across posts.** If part two only makes sense after part one, they are one post.
85	
86	A file may still hold several posts separated by `---`, and that is a batch of independent posts, never a sequence. Each one stands alone and the reader can meet them in any order. A post regenerated from a Substack Note is the exception: that file holds exactly one post, because the pairing is one to one.
87	
88	Length is a reach decision, not a rule. Short travels further, so stay short by default. Run long when the material is a system dump, or when the post carries its matching Note in full. Count the characters against 25,000 rather than estimating.
89	
90	## Shapes. Pick one per tweet, never blend, rotate across a set
91	
92	A set of 15 tweets that all use the same shape is one tweet written 15 times. Rotate deliberately. You cannot write a greentext about a study, which is the point: the shape forces different thinking.
93	
94	**One-liner / nuke.** One sentence, no context, complete on its own.
95	`your CI pipeline being green doesn't mean the code works`
96	
97	**Deadpan.** States something absurd like everyone already knows it. The flat delivery is the joke.
98	`running the same claude opus prompt 8 times because "maybe this time"`
99	
100	**Staircase.** Lines get shorter, weight falls on the last one. White space does the work.
101	```
102	1,000 google searches
103	415 produce a click
104	360 land on a site google doesn't own
105	
106	that's the open web's entire share
107	```
108	
109	**Reverse pyramid.** Wide, then narrow, then one line that implodes.
110	
111	**Greentext.** `>` lines, sequential, self-deprecating, ends `>mfw`. For things that went wrong. Write the arrow as a literal `>`, never as `>`, because the scorer reads the entity's semicolon as a banned semicolon and fails the file on one CRIT per line.
112	```
113	>read that video outperforms
114	>buy a camera
115	>learn premiere
116	>post to linkedin
117	>reaches 10x fewer people than plain text
118	>mfw
119	```
120	
121	**Fragment.** Trails off. Lets the reader finish it.
122	`prompt caching exists and you're just...`
123	
124	**Cocky take.** No hedging, no "in my experience". States it confidently. Invites the quote-tweet disagreement, which is free distribution.
125	`if your AI output sounds generic you gave it nothing. the model is fine. you are the problem.`
126	
127	**Dry flex.** An achievement stated so flatly the lack of celebration is the flex.
128	
129	**Shower thought.** Sounds offhand, cuts deep, makes people stop.
130	`"direct traffic" is your analytics tool saying "i don't know."`
131	
132	**Story beat.** One real specific moment. No lesson attached to the end.
133	
134	**Heuristic.** Name the trigger, name the correction, give the direction. The reader can run it tomorrow. Strongest shape in the mined corpus, so reach for it more than you think.
135	
136	**Field note.** One mundane place or moment used as a sensor for a large trend. Dated, specific, and it stops before the lesson.
137	
138	**Timestamped contrast.** Two dates, two lines, no commentary. `2008: build an app / 2023: build an app store`
139	
140	**Dialogue.** A short transcript where the contradiction accuses the subject for you. One calm line of commentary after, at most.
141	
142	**System dump.** The long post that lists a real working setup step by step. Every step names a tool and a trigger, every number is real, and it never closes on "comment X and I'll DM you". The shape most likely to run long, since X Premium+ now carries that length in the post itself.
143	
144	Match shape to energy: hurts because true → one-liner or shower thought. Embarrassing → greentext or story beat. Can't believe it works this way → deadpan or fragment. Stating it without apology → cocky take. The visual has to land → staircase or pyramid.
145	
146	## Voice
147	
148	Lowercase reads casual and confident. Fragments are fine when the meaning is clear. No hedging, no "in my experience", no "this is just me". Specificity beats generality every time, so write "4 years" and "$340", never "a long time" and "a lot". Dark humor is fair game and self-deprecation earns trust. Silence the editor that wants to explain the joke.
149	
150	## Hard bans
151	
152	**Hook shapes:** "Unpopular opinion:", "Hot take:", "Nobody talks about this", "I used to think X. I was wrong.", "Steal this", "[Year] taught me [lesson]", "Here's what I learned:", "A thread 🧵". Also never open on a question, per Voice.md.
153	
154	**Thread furniture:** `1/`, `2/`, `🧵`, "thread below", "more in the replies", and any pinned-comment line. All four are retired, see the one-post rule above.
155	
156	**Closers:** "What do you think?", "Drop your thoughts below", "Tag someone who needs this", "Follow me for more", "Retweet if you agree", "Save this".
157	
158	**Constructions:** the banned words, the negative parallelism forms and the tricolon cap are all in `slop_rules.py`, already in context. The copula dodge and the other shapes sit in section 1 of `core/pattern-rules.md`. Do not restate either list here, and do not treat the absence of a restatement as permission.
159	
160	**AI tells specific to X:** perfect symmetry between setup and payoff, every tweet ending on a lesson, a clean three-act structure inside one tweet, explaining the joke in the last line. None of these four is in the scorer, so they are checked by reading.
161	
162	## The judge pass. Score your own drafts before he sees them
163	
164	Run this after the drafts exist and before the six mechanical checks. Score every tweet out of 5 on each axis, print the table, and rewrite anything below 18. Judging your own work feels redundant and it is the step that catches the three failures a read-through never does.
165	
166	| Axis | 5 looks like | 1 looks like |
167	|---|---|---|
168	| Claim | He would defend this in a reply thread | A fact with no position on it |
169	| Specificity | Names, numbers, exact strings | "the best people", "a lot", "recently" |
170	| Register | Sounds like him out loud | Sounds like a caption |
171	| Standalone | Works with every other tweet covered | Needs the set to make sense |
172	| Shape fidelity | Matches the shape's real mechanic | Wears the shape's label only |
173	
174	Three failure modes score low every time, so hunt them by name.
175	
176	**The vague superlative.** "the four sharpest people i read", "one of the best threads", "a huge corpus". You have the names and the numbers in the material you were handed, so put them in. @nabeelqu's heuristic works because it quotes the exact sentence that triggers it. Any superlative without a name attached is an unfinished draft.
177	
178	**Rhythm beating accuracy.** A line that scans better than the truth. Merging two tools into one, rounding a cost up, saying "paid" about something free. Every factual claim traces back to something that actually happened, and the version that scans worse ships.
179	
180	**The borrowed line as payload.** Quoting someone else's sentence and letting it carry the tweet. The reader remembers them, not him. Quote someone only when your own take is the larger half, and never as the closing line.
181	
182	## Before you hand it over
183	
184	Run all nine. A failure on any one means rewrite, not ship.
185	
186	1. **First six words of every tweet.** Any that name a source get rewritten.
187	2. **Shape rotation.** No two consecutive tweets share a shape, and no set leans on one shape.
188	3. **Negative parallelism scan.** Search every draft for the word "not" and for "isn't". Any tweet built as `X. not Y.` or as `this is not X, it is Y` gets rewritten to say Y on its own. This is the single most common construction that survives a first draft, so scan for it by hand rather than trusting a read-through.
189	4. **Character count.** The ceiling is 25,000 characters, not 280, because Atharva is on X Premium+. Count characters, do not estimate. Most posts still stay short, because a short post reads better and travels further.
190	5. **Thread scan.** Search every draft for `1/`, for `🧵`, and for the word "thread". Any hit is a rewrite into one post. Search for "pinned" as well, because that mechanic belongs to LinkedIn.
191	   **Link scan.** Search for `http`. Any hit comes out, including a link to his own blog. Search for "link in" too.
192	6. **Standalone check.** Cover every other post in the file. Does this one still work alone?
193	7. **Scorer.** `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` and CRIT must reach 0. Ignore the flow, paragraph and fragment findings, which are long-form rules that do not apply to short-form.
194	
195	Run `python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"` as well, and take CRIT to 0. It asks whether a reader outside this vault can follow the piece. Every CRIT names a term coined here, so searching the web gives the reader the wrong meaning and only a gloss on the page fixes it. A PostToolUse hook blocks the write while a CRIT stands.
196	8. **Pattern rules.** Section 7 of `core/pattern-rules.md`, run after the scorer. Then section 6 of the same file, because a set of tweets edited flat is worse than a set with one tell left in it.
197	9. **Uniqueness.** `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md`, five questions. A tweet that fails question 1 (his frame, not just the fact) or question 5 (would any other account post this) does not ship.
198	
199	## Output order
200	
201	Show the take table, then the drafts, then the judge table with the rewrites already applied. Hand him the scored set rather than a first pass, because a draft he has to grade himself is work you moved onto his desk.
202	
203	## Where the file goes
204	
205	Check for an existing placeholder before writing anything. One file per topic per channel, never duplicate, never write outside `SOCIALS/Tweets/`.
206	
207	Look for `SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_[Exact Blog Title].md`. If it exists, write into it. If it does not, create it.
208	
209	```markdown
210	---
211	type: Tweet
212	title: Exact Blog Title
213	source_blog: "[[Exact Blog Title]]"
214	description: "The hook, one line"
215	created: YYYY-MM-DD
216	updated: YYYY-MM-DD
217	posted: false
218	---
219	
220	[the post, immediately, nothing between it and the frontmatter]
221	```
222	
223	A post regenerated from a Substack Note carries `series` and `sequence` copied from that Note, because those two fields are what pair the file to it.
224	
225	Use `source_blog: none` for original content with no source article. Never emit a `#tweet` tag and never emit a `**Source Blog:**` line, both retired 2026-07-27. Never put an extra `---` between the frontmatter and the post, because a stray one reads as a block break.
226	
227	One file usually holds one post. A batch file may hold several independent posts separated by `---` on its own line, and the review desk shows each as its own card. Never number them, because they are not a sequence. A file paired to a Note holds exactly one post.
228	
229	## Output
230	
231	Show the take table, then the tweets. Add one line on why a shape fits only where it is genuinely interesting. Skip emoji headers, skip a "WHY THIS WORKS" section, skip the recap.
